The next M3 modelling tasks are RF deposition and the pedestal boundary. They need different
outputs from turbulent transport: heating profiles in the plasma volume, and values describing
the edge. Their software interfaces are now built.

## A complete source profile

The RF guard checks inputs, output bounds and ensemble spread. Its default decision selects a
complete source profile. Mixing surrogate values at some radii with fallback values at others
can change the integrated heating power, even when each profile separately has the right power.
An explicit physics check can reject a candidate whose volume integral is wrong. Selecting
the whole profile does not itself enforce power conservation.

A separate vector guard handles boundary responses, with units and physics criteria supplied
by the caller. Both guards retain a Tier A fallback and isolate rejected surrogate branches
from derivatives. The core loop records source spread and fallback use.

The dataset interface stores case responses or complete radial profiles. Related launches,
equilibria or trajectories share a group identifier and stay together in training or holdout
sets. Source hashes, units, reference version, failures and the split seed are recorded.
Radial profiles keep their supplied toroidal-flux coordinate; there is no silent conversion
from poloidal flux.

The synthetic software checks give [25 synthetic contract tests pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-143](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-143){.cid .st-tested}. Nonfinite Gaussian RF parameters are
also rejected: [12 nonfinite-parameter cases pass in each mode]{.claim}[C-144](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-144){.cid .st-tested}. These tests establish interface behaviour, not prediction
accuracy for an RF or pedestal model.

## The reference comes next

The existing RF baseline is an analytic Gaussian EC source. The pedestal baseline takes
prescribed values. Training against these would demonstrate a pipeline, but would not add
predictive physics. Choosing reference solvers or data is the next modelling decision.

After that choice: label grouped cases, inspect a baseline, set accuracy targets, train the
ensembles, integrate them into TORAX, and check coupled derivatives, balance and cost.
No RF/pedestal model has been trained in this step.
